actor_population.observed: each iteration reads a runtime-array byte, skips bit 20 entries, uses low 5 bits as an index into the team data path, then advances actor and source positions

active_player_mask.observed: for each team, entries after the configured active-player count are ORed with bit 20 and remaining entries are ANDed with DF; slot zero of each 20-byte array is not traversed by this routine

trajectory_selection_compare.guard: runs only when the player-setting value is below 4 and the corresponding trajectory block 1E6C/1E6E is non-negative
trajectory_selection_compare.comparison: CODE_83:C74F scans 11 byte positions, excludes current entries with bit 20, compares current against snapshot, and writes byte selection results through the supplied trajectory-block pointer

limitations: The arrays are runtime state and may be modified after initialization; this does not freeze a final formation or lineup.
The low-five-bit index, bit-20 activity mask, and trajectory comparison are structural observations, not player-number, control, pass, or shot semantics.
The byte offsets written by CODE_83:C74F have not been given gameplay labels; this extraction does not identify a trajectory as a pass or shot.
No web roster movement or actor spawning behavior is changed from this extraction alone.
